_meta.description: Real retrieval output captured from the Discovery 'cardiology-canon' GraphRAG shelf (provider graphrag-zero, 545 docs) via the bookshelf search/ask tools. This file is the agent->notebook bridge: the Jupyter kernel cannot call the stdio MCP GraphRAG tool directly, so genuine query results are persisted here and loaded by the retrieval-integration cell in af-rotor-mechanisms-workflow.ipynb.
_meta.honest_note: The cardiology-canon corpus is composed of clinical guidelines and outcome trials (anticoagulation, ablation-vs-drug, HF, dyslipidemia). It contains NO rotor/driver basic-science (optical mapping, calcium alternans, anisotropic conduction-velocity, ganglionated-plexi mapping). Only Fibrosis topology and Inflammation/coupling could be substantiated at a guideline/association level. The other three mechanisms returned no direct evidence and are recorded as unsupported so the evidence gate can correctly flag them for requery.

supporting_evidence.claim: Enlarged atrial size and/or atrial fibrosis mark patients at higher risk of AF recurrence and are relevant to ablation candidacy and substrate-directed, personalized rhythm control.

supporting_evidence.claim: Non-invasive substrate characterization (echocardiography/MRI/CT) alongside clinical factors is proposed to individualize rhythm-control strategy selection.

conflicting_evidence.claim: Randomized ablation trials show only modest long-term reductions in AF burden, indicating that substrate/fibrosis targeting alone does not guarantee durable rhythm control.
conflicting_evidence.source_title: 2012 - MANTRA-PAF - Ablation as initial therapy in pAF - NEJM.pdf
conflicting_evidence.source_id: 2012 - MANTRA-PAF - Ablation as initial therapy in pAF - NEJM.pdf
conflicting_evidence.direct_quote: There was no significant difference in the cumulative burden of atrial fibrillation over the 2-year follow-up period.

confounders: AF phenotype and chronicity (paroxysmal vs persistent)
Imaging modality and thresholding used to quantify fibrosis
Fibrosis topology.key_gap: Corpus provides guideline-level associations only; no mechanistic (LGE-MRI wavefront / conduction) evidence linking fibrosis topology to rotor anchoring.

Inflammation/coupling.key_gap: Corpus supports an epidemiologic inflammation-AF association only; no direct connexin/gap-junction coupling or tissue-level electrophysiology evidence.

Anisotropy gradients.key_gap: No direct evidence in cardiology-canon. Targeted search returned only ablation-technique and guideline chunks; the corpus contains no conduction-velocity/anisotropic-propagation basic science.
Anisotropy gradients.requery_prompt: Ingest electrophysiology literature on anisotropic conduction velocity, fiber orientation, and rotor drift, then re-query.

Calcium instability.key_gap: No direct evidence in cardiology-canon. Search returned inherited-conduction-disease and HCM chunks; no calcium-alternans / SR-release wavebreak studies exist in the corpus.
Calcium instability.requery_prompt: Ingest cellular-electrophysiology literature on intracellular calcium handling, alternans, and afterdepolarizations, then re-query.

Autonomic heterogeneity.key_gap: No direct evidence in cardiology-canon. Search returned bradycardia/conduction-delay and general AF-management chunks; no ganglionated-plexi / autonomic-mapping studies exist in the corpus.
Autonomic heterogeneity.requery_prompt: Ingest autonomic-nervous-system and ganglionated-plexi ablation literature, then re-query.
